ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are 6 junctions: vertex B; two junctions in the middle, left and right; the bottom-left junction; the bottom-middle junction; the bottom-right end is labeled A. It can be seen that there are 9 paths in total: B to middle-left, B to middle-right, middle-left to middle-right, middle-left to bottom-left, bottom-left to bottom-middle, middle-left to bottom-middle, middle-right to bottom-middle, middle-right to A, bottom-middle to A. Each path length is 100 m. Reasoning: Regard the figure as a graph in graph theory. The degrees of the points are: A is connected to bottom-middle and middle-right, degree 2; B is connected to middle-left and middle-right, degree 2; bottom-left is connected to middle-left and bottom-middle, degree 2; middle-left, middle-right, and bottom-middle are each connected to 4 edges, and their degrees are all 4. So the complete 9 edges form a graph in which all vertex degrees are even, and it can have an Euler circuit, but if all 9 edges are used, the route must return to the starting point and cannot start from A and end at B. If one wants to go from A to B without repeating edges, the trail formed by the used edges should have only A and B as odd-degree vertices. If only 1 edge is not used, that is, 8 edges are used, then the two endpoints of the deleted edge will become odd-degree vertices. To make the odd-degree vertices exactly A and B, an edge directly connecting A and B must be deleted, but there is no direct A-B edge in the figure, so 8 edges is impossible. Two edges can be deleted, for example deleting A to middle-right and middle-right to B. The remaining 7 edges can still form a trail from A to B, for example: A → bottom-middle → middle-right → middle-left → bottom-middle → bottom-left → middle-left → B. In this way there is no repeated path, and 7 paths are traveled in total. Therefore the longest distance is 7 × 100 m = 700 m.

raw_record.question_text: Each of the nine paths in a park are $100 \mathrm{~m}$ long. Anna wants to walk from $A$ to $B$ without using the same path twice. How long is the longest path she can choose?

method.method_draft: Model the picture as a graph. From the image, read the six junctions: bottom-left, bottom-middle, A at bottom-right, mid-left, mid-right, and B at the top. The nine visible paths are the graph edges. Count degrees: A has degree 2, B has degree 2, the bottom-left vertex has degree 2, and the three central/mid vertices each have degree 4, so all vertices have even degree. Since all 9 edges form an Euler circuit, a route using all 9 edges would have to start and end at the same vertex, not start at A and end at B. For a trail from A to B, the used-edge subgraph must have exactly A and B as odd-degree vertices. Using 8 edges would mean omitting one edge; that would make the endpoints of the omitted edge odd, but there is no direct A-B edge in the image, so 8 edges is impossible. Omitting two edges along a two-edge route from A to B, for example A--mid-right and mid-right--B, leaves 7 edges with only A and B odd and still connected enough to trace as a trail. Therefore the maximum is 7 paths, and since each path is 100 m, the longest distance is 700 m.

图像描述：图中有 6 个 junction：顶点 B；中间左、右两个 junction；底部左 junction；底部中间 junction；底部右端标为 A。可见共有 9 条路径：B 到中左、B 到中右、中左到中右、中左到底左、底左到底中、中左到底中、中右到底中、中右到 A、底中到 A。每条路径长度都是 100 m。

推理：把图看成图论中的图。各点度数为：A 连接到底中和中右，度数 2；B 连接到中左和中右，度数 2；底左连接到中左和底中，度数 2；中左、中右、底中各连接 4 条边，度数都是 4。所以完整的 9 条边形成所有顶点度数均为偶数的图，可以有欧拉回路，但若使用全部 9 条边，路线必须回到出发点，不能从 A 出发到 B 结束。

若想从 A 到 B 且不重复边，所使用边构成的 trail 应只有 A 和 B 是奇度点。若只少用 1 条边，即使用 8 条边，则被删去那条边的两个端点会变成奇度点。要让奇度点正好是 A 和 B，就必须删去一条直接连接 A 和 B 的边，但图中没有 A-B 直接边，所以 8 条边不可能。

可以删去两条边，例如删去 A 到中右、以及中右到 B。剩下 7 条边仍能形成从 A 到 B 的 trail，例如：A → 底中 → 中右 → 中左 → 底中 → 底左 → 中左 → B。这样没有重复路径，共走 7 条路径。因此最长距离是 7 × 100 m = 700 m。
